strengths: Clear problem motivation addressing real limitations of existing extrapolative NVS methods
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Co3D, DTU, RealEstate10K) with appropriate baselines and both interpolative and extrapolative settings
Strong empirical results showing state-of-the-art performance on extrapolative view synthesis with good zero-shot generalization
Well-motivated cross-modal attention distillation mechanism with clear visual justification (Figure 3)
Flexible architecture that generalizes to variable numbers of input views despite 2-view training
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component
Practical technical contributions including proximity-based mesh conditioning and camera-space coordinate normalization
weaknesses: Table 5 (depth prediction accuracy) is explicitly marked incomplete ('under experiment being filled'), representing critical missing geometry evaluation despite claims of significant geometry contributions
Heavy dependency on VGGT geometry predictor with ground truth geometry from VGGT predictions during training, creating a closed-loop that limits generalization to other predictors
Cross-modal attention design (Eq. 7) lacks theoretical justification—why asymmetrically share K,Q but not V? Why not explore alternative distillation approaches?
No computational cost analysis provided (training time, inference time, memory requirements) despite training on 3 large datasets
Camera-space pointmap normalization shows dramatic improvements (Figure 9) but is relegated to appendix; unclear if included in main ablation (Table 3)
Missing comparison with relevant method CAT3D [6] despite inclusion in references; limited analysis of failure modes and scene type limitations

Limited novelty in individual components (warping-and-inpainting from prior work, geometry conditioning established by GenWarp); main novelty is cross-modal attention which shows modest improvement (~0.03 LPIPS)
Geometry evaluation primarily via depth metrics rather than 3D reconstruction quality; no comparison with dedicated depth prediction methods or standard 3D benchmarks

strengths: Well-motivated pose-free novel view synthesis problem with clear practical applications and elegant solution to ensure image-geometry alignment
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) with both zero-shot and in-domain evaluation, including extensive ablations and robustness tests
Strong empirical results, particularly for extrapolative view synthesis (SOTA in extrapolation: 17.41 PSNR vs 14.36 for NoPoSplat), with efficient inference (9.67s vs 209.19s for ViewCrafter)
Clear technical contributions including cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI), proximity-based mesh conditioning, and camera-space normalization, each with demonstrated benefits
Excellent reproducibility emphasis with detailed implementation details, promised code/weights release, and strong documentation of methods and hyperparameters
Good architectural design enabling variable input views, image-only inference mode, and geometric alignment without scale-shift fitting
weaknesses: Limited core novelty—primarily engineering contribution building incrementally on well-established warping-and-inpainting methods (LucidDreamer, GenWarp); MoAI's core mechanism (attention map swapping) is conceptually simple without deeper theoretical insight

Heavy dependency on external VGGT geometry predictor limits novelty scope; essentially a wrapper combining existing components; 'pose-free' claim is somewhat misleading as poses are still estimated externally
Insufficient analysis of why MoAI works beyond intuitive Fig. 3 motivation; lacks investigation of alternative designs (reverse instillation, partial transfer); mechanism appears somewhat heuristic

Significant geometry evaluation gaps: lacks quantitative metrics (depth accuracy, point cloud errors) on standard benchmarks; evaluation primarily visual; no comparison of geometry quality to depth-focused methods or user studies validating alignment
Conservative extrapolation evaluation with limited systematic analysis of extreme view differences; no discussion of failure modes or scene types where method struggles
Critical implementation detail (camera-space pointmap normalization) buried in appendix despite Fig. 8 showing substantial performance impact; should be elevated to main paper
Scalability concerns: training with batch size 1, 28GB memory for joint generation, unclear how method scales to higher resolutions or larger-scale scenes

Limited generalization analysis: evaluation concentrated on indoor/object-centric scenes; minimal outdoor and large-scale evaluation; no systematic analysis of challenging scenarios (transparency, thin structures, dynamic content)
